execution.observed: 19 of 20 natural completions; 1 reasoning-only truncation at 16384; stop rule fired

identity.reason: A different output ceiling is a different workload identity. This plan does not mutate the 8192 study or the 1024 plan.

authorization.authorized_by: Owner session goal: "Complete all performance benchmarks"
authorization.scope: One 20-request cell at concurrency 1, 10,240 requested input tokens, 16384-token output ceiling, against the configured deployment.
authorization.note: This authorization covers only this pilot cell. It does not authorize a multiwindow run, a further ceiling increase, or any qualification claim.

review_of_prior_runs.multiwindow_8192_cell: run-6cabf9e5ee70-w1-c1 censored 2 of 20, both reasoning-only at 8192.
review_of_prior_runs.gap: The 8192 outliers' stopping point is still unobserved. 16384 is a 2x probe above the first censoring cap.

design.wall_time_basis: The 8192 pilot took 58 s and the censored 8192 cell took 87 s. A worst case where every request reaches 16384 at roughly 100 output tokens/s would take about 55 minutes.

continue_only_if: actual HTTP attempts equal planned requests
validated engine schema and raw evidence present
provider-versus-target conformance within the profile tolerance
stop_rule.on_failure: Stop. Preserve artifacts. Do not raise the cap automatically. Do not run a multiwindow at this ceiling. Review the evidence and change the design or the stop rule only through a new owner decision.
prohibited: merging this run with the 8192 or 2048 studies
treating a clean 20-request pilot as ceiling certification
stop_rule.interpretation_limit: A clean 20-request cell does not certify 16384 and does not show that a 240-request zero-censoring gate will pass. It only permits consideration of a separately versioned multiwindow design.

cost.note: Client-side conservative bound assuming every request reaches 16384. Actual spend is expected to be far lower. Not a provider billing limit.

next_after_clean_pilot.description: A separately versioned multiwindow design at 16384. The zero-censoring stop rule remains statistically fragile even if this pilot is clean; changing it requires an owner decision.
